questions.prompt: A service times out, but the downstream operation might still complete later.
questions.explanation: Treat timeout as unknown outcome and make retries idempotent. In DDIA: Trouble with Distributed Systems, the first move is to protect the system's real guarantee: expect partial failure.
options: Treat timeout as unknown outcome and make retries idempotent
questions.answer: Treat timeout as unknown outcome and make retries idempotent

concept_panel.title: Partial Failure in Distributed Systems
concept_panel.explanation: Distributed systems can fail partially: one node may be alive while the network drops messages, pauses a process, or delays responses. A timeout means the result is unknown, not definitely failed. Retries can duplicate work unless operations are idempotent. Leases need fencing tokens because paused processes can resume after their authority expired.
key_takeaways: Fencing tokens protect against stale lease holders.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand distributed systems failures and uncertainty.
concept_panel.practical_example: A payment request times out but later succeeds, so a retry without an idempotency key can double-charge.
